'''Miguel Ángel''' "'''Míchel'''" '''Salgado Fernández''' (born 22 October 1975) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[right-back]].

Nicknamed ''Il Due''<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/papel/2005/01/22/deportes/1747116.html|title=Diez años de ''Il Due''|trans-title=Ten years of ''Il Due''|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=22 January 2005|access-date=4 April 2009}}</ref> ("two" in Italian), he was known for his combative tackling and attacking play. After excellent displays at [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta]], he spent an entire decade at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], where former teammate [[Steve McManaman]] attested to his aggressive style by describing him as "the hardest person in the world....a genuine psychopath, even in training."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/clubs/premier-league/blackburn-rovers/10-things-you-didn-t-know-about-Miguel-Salgado-article109539.html|title=10 things you didn't know about Miguel Salgado|newspaper=[[Daily Mirror]]|last=Aikman|first=Richard|date=11 August 2009|access-date=25 August 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120005042/http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/clubs/premier-league/blackburn-rovers/10-things-you-didn-t-know-about-Miguel-Salgado-article109539.html|archive-date=20 January 2012}}</ref> He also played three seasons in England with [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]].

Salgado, who played 343 [[La Liga]] matches and scored seven goals, represented the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]] over eight years, collecting more than 50 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] and appearing in one [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] and one [[UEFA European Championship|European Championship]].

==Club career==
===Celta===
Born in [[As Neves]], [[Province of Pontevedra]], [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eldebate.com/deportes/futbol/la-liga/20220402/michel-salgado.html|title=Míchel Salgado, el celtiña que debutó ante el Madrid y acabó convertido en leyenda blanca|trans-title=Míchel Salgado, the Celta man who made debut against Madrid and eventually became a white legend|publisher=[[El Debate (Spain)|El Debate]]|first=David|last=Vicente Casado|language=es|date=2 April 2022|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> Salgado began his professional career with hometown's [[RC Celta de Vigo]],<ref name=Celta>{{cite web|url=http://www.yojugueenelcelta.com/2008/04/michel-salgado.html|title=Míchel Salgado|publisher=Yo Jugué en el Celta|language=es|date=3 April 2008|access-date=12 June 2014}}</ref> making his [[La Liga]] debut on 22 January 1995 in a 4–0 away loss against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/gradario/hemeroteca/2017/01/22/cumplen-22-anos-debut-michel-salgado-celta/00031485082257032771510.htm|title=Se cumplen 22 años del debut de Míchel Salgado con el Celta|trans-title=22 years of Míchel Salgado's debut with Celta|newspaper=[[La Voz de Galicia]]|language=es|date=22 January 2017|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref> He was loaned for a season to [[UD Salamanca]] in the [[Segunda División]], and after his return became the first-choice in his position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2016/08/23/celta-de-vigo/685832-suena-michel-michel-salgado.html|title=Suena Míchel, Míchel Salgado|trans-title=The man of the hour is Míchel, Míchel Salgado|publisher=Vavel|last=Laborda González|first=Adrià|language=es|date=23 August 2016|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

Whilst at Celta, Salgado was involved in an incident with [[Atlético Madrid]]'s [[Juninho Paulista]] in February 1998: after a dangerous challenge, the Brazilian was sidelined for six months and missed [[1998 FIFA World Cup|that year]]'s [[FIFA World Cup]].<ref name=EURO>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/spain/squad/743428.stm|title=Miguel Salgado|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=6 October 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/1998/febrero/02/deportes/juninho.html|title=Juninho, roto|trans-title=Juninho, torn|newspaper=El Mundo|last1=Álvarez|first1=R. J.|last2=Izquierdo|first2=C. G.|language=es|date=2 February 1998|access-date=4 April 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/1998/02/19/deportes/19N0083.html|title=El Celta exige para Míchel Salgado el beneficio de la duda|trans-title=Celta demand benefit of doubt for Míchel Salgado|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=19 February 1998|access-date=4 April 2009}}</ref>

Salgado scored a career-best three goals in the [[1998–99 La Liga|1998–99 campaign]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/1998/09/27/deportes/906847203_850215.html|title=El Celta empata en el descuento|trans-title=Celta draw in injury time|newspaper=[[El País]]|last=Besa|first=Ramón|language=es|date=27 September 1998|access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/1998/12/14/deportes/913590010_850215.html|title=El Celta expone su orgullo|trans-title=Celta showcase pride|newspaper=El País|last=Campos|first=Pablo|language=es|date=14 December 1998|access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.abc.es/nav/Navigate.exe/hemeroteca/madrid/abc/1999/02/08/070.html|title=No lo tuvo tan fácil el Celta|trans-title=Celta did not have it so easy|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|language=es|date=8 February 1999|access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> helping his team to finish fifth and [[1999–2000 UEFA Cup|qualify]] for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/span99.html|title=Spain 1998/99|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|last=Adrados|first=Juan Pedro|access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref><ref name=Celta/><ref name=EURO/>

===Real Madrid===
In 1999, Salgado was purchased by Real Madrid for [[Euro|€]]11,000,000,<ref name=EURO/> playing 29 league games in his [[1999–2000 La Liga|first season]] while also helping the club [[1999–00 UEFA Champions League|win]] the [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/24/championsleague.sport1|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Valencia|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 May 2000|access-date=15 February 2016}}</ref> He was the [[Madrid|capital]] side's starter during his first seven years, but was relegated to [[Substitute (association football)|the bench]] by former [[Sevilla FC]] youngster [[Sergio Ramos]] in [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rtve.es/deportes/20090824/sentido-homenaje-salgado-bernabeu/289928.shtml|title=Sentido homenaje a Salgado en el Bernabéu|trans-title=Hearfelt homage to Salgado at the Bernabéu|publisher=[[RTVE]]|language=es|date=24 August 2009|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

[[File:Despedida de Míchel Salgado.JPG|thumb|left|Real Madrid fans show their appreciation of Salgado's ten years service to the club]]
Salgado was only able to contribute 16 matches to the ''Merengues''' 30th national title, mainly due to injuries.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2007/08/04/mas_futbol/1186178407_850215.html|title=Michel Salgado: "Quiero seguir en el Real Madrid"|trans-title=Michel Salgado: "I want to continue in Real Madrid"|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=4 August 2007|access-date=2 May 2018}}</ref> In the following two campaigns he featured very rarely (only 17 appearances), being [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] in the final game of [[2008-09 La Liga|2008–09]], a 2–1 loss at [[CA Osasuna]] on 31 May 2009 as Madrid slumped to a fifth consecutive league defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.defensacentral.com/real_madrid/29711-casillas-y-teixeira-salvan-a-osasuna-osasuna-2-1-real-madrid/|title=Casillas y Teixeira salvan a Osasuna|trans-title=Casillas and Teixeira save Osasuna|publisher=Defensa Central|last=Torrico|first=Eduardo|language=es|date=31 May 2009|access-date=15 February 2016}}</ref>

Salgado was released in early August 2009, with the team already midway into pre-season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202777494192/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/MICHEL_SALGADO_2009-08-04.htm|title=Official announcement|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=4 August 2009|access-date=4 August 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090807024936/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202777494192/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/MICHEL_SALGADO_2009-08-04.htm|archive-date=7 August 2009}}</ref>

===Blackburn Rovers===
Salgado moved to [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] of the [[Premier League]] on 19 August 2009, signing a two-year deal after impressing manager [[Sam Allardyce]] whilst on trial. He went on to say he was happy to be playing for his new club, intending to retire at [[Ewood Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blackburncitizen.co.uk/sport/4553432.Salgado_set_for_Blackburn_Rovers_move/|title=Salgado set for Blackburn Rovers|publisher=Blackburn Citizen|date=19 August 2009|access-date=19 August 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/blackburn-rovers/6055073/Blackburn-Rovers-complete-signing-of-former-Real-Madrid-full-back-Michel-Salgado.html|title=Blackburn Rovers complete signing of former Real Madrid full-back Michel Salgado|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=19 August 2009|access-date=2 October 2014}}</ref>

Salgado made his competitive debut on 12 September 2009, against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] as a late substitute (3–1 home win).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8247147.stm|title=Blackburn 3–1 Wolverhampton|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Roopanarine|first=Les|date=12 September 2009|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref> On 27 October he scored his only goal for his new team, in a [[2009–10 Football League Cup|5–2 victory]] over [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] in the [[EFL Cup|Football League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/8323055.stm|title=Blackburn 5–2 Peterborough|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 October 2009|access-date=15 February 2016}}</ref>

On 27 January 2011, the 35-year-old Salgado agreed to a contract extension.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.footballpress.net/?action=read&idsel=77946|title=Salgado happy to extend his Blackburn deal|publisher=Football Press|date=28 January 2011|access-date=16 June 2011|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110130012718/http://www.footballpress.net/?action=read&idsel=77946|archive-date=30 January 2011}}</ref> He was first choice in the first games of the [[2011–12 Premier League|2011–12 season]], until picking up an injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/grella-nelsen-still-sidelined-blackburn-rovers-1997361|title=Grella, Nelsen still sidelined for Blackburn Rovers|publisher=Tribal Football|last=Slevison|first=Andrew|date=21 October 2011|access-date=15 November 2011}}</ref>

Blackburn manager [[Steve Kean]] revealed in December 2011 that Salgado was being omitted from the squad as his contract stated that the player was entitled to a new deal if he played nine more matches in the campaign, the club not being able to afford fresh terms.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7387948/|title=Salgado 'frozen out'|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=20 December 2011|access-date=24 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/127135.html|title=Blackburn can't afford to play me – Salgado|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=20 December 2011|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

===Futsal and later years===
[[File:Míchel Salgado in Tehran.jpg|thumb|Salgado in a charity match in [[Tehran]] in 2015]]
Aged 40, Salgado came out of retirement to join Kochi 5s in India's [[Premier Futsal]] as a [[marquee player]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/136/india/2016/07/12/25561652/premier-futsal-squads-announced-for-inaugural-edition|title=Premier Futsal: Squads announced for inaugural edition|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=12 July 2016|access-date=17 July 2016}}</ref> He later was part of the board of Heritage Sports Holdings, which owned the football clubs [[Gibraltar United F.C.]] and [[UD Los Barrios]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/mas-futbol/tercera-division/2017/12/13/5a3165fcca47413e208b4689.html|title=Michel Salgado, al rescate de la UD Los Barrios de Tercera|trans-title=Michel Salgado, to the rescue of UD Los Barrios from ''Tercera''|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|last=Piñero|first=Margota|language=es|date=13 December 2017|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://hsh.football/who-we-are/|title=Who we are – Our story|publisher=Heritage Sports Holdings|access-date=7 April 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131132833/http://hsh.football/who-we-are/|archive-date=31 January 2020}}</ref>

Salgado came out of retirement again in April 2018, starting for [[C.A. Independiente de La Chorrera]] in a 1–1 draw against [[C.D. Plaza Amador]] in the quarter-finals of the [[2017–18 Liga Panameña de Fútbol season|Panamanian Clausura tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2018/04/29/internacional/1524970634_622765.html|title=Míchel Salgado reaparece en Panamá con un empate|trans-title=Míchel Salgado reappears in Panama with a draw|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=29 April 2018|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref> He settled in [[Dubai]], [[United Arab Emirates]] after retiring, and in 2020 helped to found [[Fursan Hispania FC]], initially as an academy.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/football/michel-salgado-admits-to-feeling-nervous-ahead-of-watching-fursan-hispania-in-action-1.1142644|title=Michel Salgado admits to feeling 'nervous' ahead of watching Fursan Hispania in action|newspaper=[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National]]|last=Passela|first=Amith|date=8 January 2021|access-date=14 July 2024}}</ref>

On 5 February 2021, Salgado was appointed [[director of football]] of [[Cypriot First Division]] side [[Pafos FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.onsports.gr/podosfairo/story/714684/episimi-i-vomva-stin-kypro-thryliki-morfi-tis-real-madritis-photos|title=Επίσημη η "βόμβα" – Στην Κύπρο θρυλική μορφή της Ρεάλ Μαδρίτης (photos)|trans-title=The "bomb" is official – Real Madrid legend in Cyprus (photos)|publisher=Onsports|language=el|date=5 February 2021|access-date=5 February 2021}}</ref> On two occasions, he acted as their [[caretaker manager]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/gradario/2023/04/10/michel-salgado-asume-forma-interina-banquillo-pafos/00031681116677995165917.htm|title=Míchel Salgado asume de forma interina el banquillo del Pafos|trans-title=Míchel Salgado takes over Pafos' bench on an interim basis|newspaper=La Voz de Galicia|language=es|date=10 April 2023|access-date=2 July 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
Salgado won the first of his 53 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2009/08/24/mas_futbol/1251064852_850215.html|title=Míchel Salgado es homenajeado en el Bernabéu tras diez años como jugador del Madrid|trans-title=Míchel Salgado is honoured at the Bernabéu after ten years as a Madrid player|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=24 August 2009|access-date=14 July 2024}}</ref> on 5 September 1998, in an infamous 3–2 loss in [[Cyprus national football team|Cyprus]] for the [[UEFA Euro 2000]] [[UEFA Euro 2000 qualifying|qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/1998/septiembre/05/deportes/futbol.html|title=España cae ante Chipre, un equipo repleto de aficionados|trans-title=Spain fall against Cyprus, team filled with amateurs|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=5 September 1998|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref> He was part of the nation's squads at Euro 2000<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/spain/759256.stm|title=Spanish squad unveiled|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 May 2000|access-date=14 July 2024}}</ref> and the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dw.com/es/espa%C3%B1a-arabia-saud%C3%AD-salgado-contra-los-hijos-del-desierto/a-2064778|title=España – Arabia Saudí: Salgado contra los "hijos del desierto"|trans-title=Spain – Saudi Arabia: Salgado against the "desert sons"|publisher=[[DW-TV]]|language=es|date=23 June 2006|access-date=15 February 2016}}</ref>

Due to last-minute injuries, Salgado missed out on the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=188686.html|title=Goodbye pharoes, hello Faro|publisher=UEFA|last=Modia|first=Iván|date=12 June 2004|access-date=1 October 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130721081539/http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=188686.html|archive-date=21 July 2013}}</ref> He also represented the [[Galicia national football team|Galician autonomous side]], which he later coached alongside [[Deportivo de La Coruña]]'s [[Fran (footballer, born 1969)|Fran]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.atlantico.net/articulo/deportes/riazor-escenario-galicia-venezuela-fran-y-michel-salgado-tecnicos/20160414114706525419.html|title=Riazor, escenario del Galicia-Venezuela con Fran y Míchel Salgado de técnicos|trans-title=Riazor, venue of Galicia-Venezuela with Fran and Míchel Salgado as managers|newspaper=[[Atlántico Diario]]|language=es|date=14 April 2016|access-date=15 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cadenaser.com/emisora/2016/05/06/radio_vigo/1462540258_564344.html|title=El Celta protagonista de la selección gallega|trans-title=Celta protagonist of Galician national team|publisher=[[Cadena SER]]|last=Montes|first=Paula|language=es|date=6 May 2016|access-date=30 April 2018}}</ref>

On 4 September 2018, Salgado was named assistant manager to the [[Egypt national football team|Egyptian national team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/michel-salgado-resumes-duty-as-egypt-assistant-coach/oejfo1i6xkwv1v7fm65u064c8|title=Michel Salgado resumes duty as Egypt assistant coach|publisher=Goal|last=Oludare|first=Shina|date=4 September 2018|access-date=28 October 2018}}</ref> In June 2024, following rumours that he would be taking over [[TFF First League]] club [[Sakaryaspor]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/internacional/michel-salgado-se-va-a-turquia-n/|title=Míchel Salgado se va a Turquía|trans-title=Míchel Salgado goes to Turkey|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Sancar|first=Özgür|language=es|date=23 June 2024|access-date=2 July 2024}}</ref> he became head coach of the [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia under-15 national team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/futbol-internacional/2024/06/28/667ed13c22601d98408b45e2.html|title=Míchel Salgado se hace cargo de la Selección Sub 15 de Arabia Saudí|trans-title=Míchel Salgado takes charge of the Saudi Arabia Under 15 national team|newspaper=Marca|last=Castro|first=Juan|language=es|date=28 June 2024|access-date=2 July 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Salgado married Malula Sanz, daughter of former Real Madrid president [[Lorenzo Sanz]], on 5 July 2000.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hola.com/famosos/2009/04/15/michel-salgado/|title=Míchel Salgado and Malula Sanz esperan su tercer hijo|trans-title=Míchel Salgado and Malula Sanz expect their third child|publisher=[[¡Hola!]]|language=es|date=15 April 2009|access-date=4 November 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090830191312/http://www.hola.com/famosos/2009/04/15/michel-salgado/|archive-date=30 August 2009}}</ref> They have three children, daughter Malu (born 2003) and sons Miguel (2005) and Alán (2009).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.abc.es/estilo/gente/abci-michel-salgado-y-malula-sanz-seran-padres-tercera-200904200300-92280438016_noticia.html|title=Michel Salgado y Malula Sanz serán padres por tercera vez|trans-title=Michel Salgado and Malula Sanz will be parents for the third time|newspaper=ABC|language=es|date=20 April 2009|access-date=2 July 2024}}</ref> Malu is a singer,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20210413302339/malu-hija-michel-salgado-carrera-cantante/|title=Malu, la hija de Míchel Salgado y nieta de Lorenzo Sanz, comienza su carrera como cantante|trans-title=Malu, Míchel Salgado's daughter and Lorenzo Sanz's granddaughter, starts her singing career|publisher=¡Hola!|last=Suero|first=Enrique|language=es|date=13 April 2021|access-date=2 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20231017351583/malu-hija-michel-salgado-cantante-primeros-pasos-musica/|title=Malu, la hija de Míchel Salgado, nos habla de sus
